name: Sintashta and Andronovo
place: the southern Urals and the steppes of Kazakhstan
desc: Herders and metalworkers of the steppe who built round fortified towns with a furnace in every house and buried their chiefs with the first spoked-wheel chariots. Their way of life spread from the Urals to the Altai and down toward Iran and India.
source: Excavations at Sintashta (from 1972) and Arkaim (from 1987); graves with chariots at Sintashta and Krivoye Ozero

belligerent: drove a two-horse chariot faster than any rider could follow
cautious: smelted copper in the furnace under my own house
gluttonous: brought a hundred horses through the snow to the winter pastures

inventions.name: Spoked-Wheel Chariot
inventions.source: Chariots with spoked wheels buried at Sintashta and Krivoye Ozero, c. 2000 BCE, are the oldest known
inventions.desc: A light car on two spoked wheels, drawn by two horses at a gallop: +2 attack, everyone travels 5% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication and Polished Stone Tools.

inventions.name: A Furnace in Every House
inventions.source: At Arkaim and Sintashta nearly every house had its own well and copper-smelting furnace
inventions.desc: Each family smelts its own copper from green stone in a furnace beside the well: quarrying 15% faster, +1 attack.

inventions.name: The Round Town
inventions.source: Arkaim: two rings of houses and walls around a central square, about 160 m across
inventions.desc: Houses built back to back in two rings inside a ditch and a wall, all doors facing the middle: +2 defence, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Great Horse Herds
inventions.source: Horse bones dominate Sintashta and Andronovo sites; horses were also sacrificed in the chiefs' graves
inventions.desc: Herds of horses for milk, meat, riding and the chariot: the stores hold 20 more, everyone carries 1 more.

foods.name: Mare's Milk
foods.source: Fat residues in pots from Botai (c. 3500 BCE) show that mares were milked on the steppe very early
foods.desc: Milk from the herd's mares, fresh or soured: hunger grows 10% slower, +1 mood.

foods.name: Smoked River Fish
foods.desc: Fish from the steppe rivers smoked over the house fires for winter: food spoils 10% slower.

finds.name: Malachite Seams
finds.source: The Sintashta people mined copper ores such as malachite in the southern Urals
finds.desc: Banded green stone that turns into copper in the furnace.

finds.name: Steppe Pasture
finds.desc: Rich grass stretching to the sky, where horse herds grow. Finding it brings domestication closer.

people.name: Ziya
people.desc: Her furnace gives the cleanest copper in the town.
memory: cast twelve sickles in one day at the house furnace

people.name: Asva
people.desc: He talks to his two horses as if they were his sons.
memory: won the chariot race at the chief's funeral

people.name: The Charioteer of Sintashta
people.source: Chariot graves of the Sintashta cemetery, c. 2000 BCE
people.desc: A warrior buried with his chariot, his weapons and his two horses, the oldest charioteer we know.

people.name: The Builders of Arkaim
people.source: Arkaim, c. 2000 BCE, found in 1987 just before it was to be flooded by a reservoir
people.desc: The families who built a town in two perfect rings on the steppe, which burned, and was found again four thousand years later.

people.name: Turbin
people.source: The Seima-Turbino phenomenon: superb bronze spearheads and knives that spread across Eurasia from the Altai around 2000 BCE
people.text: a smith from the far forests of the east, whose spearheads are cast hollow in a single piece.
memory: cast a socketed spearhead that no one else could copy
people.desc: A travelling bronze-caster of the Seima-Turbino kind.

people.name: Rathin
people.label: Rathin, Lord of Chariots
people.desc: The finest charioteer of the steppe. Combat 8, very fast.

people.name: Mys
people.label: Mys, the Copper Queen
people.desc: She can find copper by the colour of the grass. Crafting 8.

people.name: Kuyash
people.label: Kuyash, Watcher of the Sky Wheel
people.desc: He reads the turning of the stars like the turning of a wheel. Lore 8.

events.title: Horses for the Chief's Journey
events.source: Sintashta chiefs were buried with chariots and with pairs of horses
events.text: The war chief has died. The elders say he must have his chariot and his two horses in the grave, so he can drive across the sky to the land of the fathers.

options.label: Give him his chariot and horses
options.result: The chariot goes into the grave with its horses. The whole steppe will hear of this burial.

options.label: Keep the horses for the living
options.result: He is buried with a model wheel. The horses graze on.

events.title: The Round Town Burns
events.source: Arkaim and several Sintashta towns were destroyed by fire
events.text: Fire has swept from house to house around the ring. The people stand on the steppe watching the smoke. Rebuild, or take to the wagons?

options.label: Rebuild the ring
options.result: The ring rises again, just as it was.

options.label: Take to the wagons
options.result: The people go back to the life of the herds, and spread far across the steppe.

events.title: The Wheel of the Sky
events.source: Some have claimed Arkaim was an observatory; most archaeologists doubt it
events.text: A wheelwright looks up at the night sky turning around the still star in the north, and sees a great wheel with spokes of light. The singers begin to call the sun a chariot.

tales.name: The Chariot of the Sun
tales.source: A shared Indo-European image: the Vedic Surya, the Greek Helios, the Trundholm sun chariot of Denmark
tales.text: Every morning the sun climbs into its golden chariot behind the eastern edge of the steppe, and its horses run across the sky all day without tiring. At night it drives under the earth and comes up again in the east. That is why our chiefs ride to their graves in chariots.

tales.name: The First Spoked Wheel
tales.source: A story made up around the invention of the spoked wheel
tales.text: A smith's daughter watched her father bend a birch rim around a fire and said: why make the wheel heavy as a stone, when the sun has only rays? She cut out the solid planks and set in thin spokes like the sun's. The new wheel was so light that the horses flew.

tales.name: The Mountain of Green Stone
tales.source: A story in the manner of Ural mining legends
tales.text: In the mountain lives a woman made of green stone, who shows the veins of copper only to those who are honest and patient. Greedy miners find nothing but rock; the patient find seams that run for years.

tales.name: The Race Around the Kurgan
tales.source: A story made up around steppe funeral games
tales.text: When the grass is high, the chariots gather at the great mound and race three times around it, so close that the wheels throw up the earth of the grave. The winner pours mare's milk on the mound for the chief who sleeps inside.
tales.moral: the living race for the dead
